prompt:
Transparent atlas, EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS AND ONE ROW. Four orthographic EDGE ELEVATIONS of the SAME horizontal rectangular orange-brick floor tile with ONE pale stone curb along only the tile's fixed right-hand long side. The four columns left-to-right are FRONT, RIGHT, LEFT, REAR. Every one of the four cells must show a very shallow horizontal edge profile; not one cell may show a square plan or a top-down view. Each object spans the same width and has the same shared slab height and baseline, with generous transparent margin. Use direct front, right, left and rear axis-aligned cameras at the tile's edge height; no perspective, no tilt, no isometric projection.

Match source: a flat rectangle of dark burnt-orange square pavers with dark mortar, with one line of pale tan weathered curb stones along the RIGHT edge in the source TOP orientation. Fixed world orientation: FRONT sees a plain orange edge with a short pale curb end-cap at the screen-right end; RIGHT sees the long pale curb side face as a shallow band; LEFT sees plain orange edge with no curb; REAR sees plain orange edge with the curb end-cap at screen-left. Only the shallow vertical outward faces are visible; top paver pattern is fully occluded. Keep attached orange masonry slab and curb with consistent Z. Preserve original warm textured brick and pale stone appearance, dark seams and age. No added raised blocks or posts.

Negative: no overhead tile plan, no broad patterned top surface, no oblique angle, no perspective, no upright wall, no corner post, no curb on the wrong edge, no duplicate curb, no loose pieces, no ground or background, no words or dividers.
